excerpt: Our Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) is our voluntary framework for managing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems.
paraphrase: The RSP is described as Anthropic's voluntary framework for managing catastrophic AI risks.

excerpt: It establishes how we identify and evaluate risks, how we make decisions about AI development and deployment, and, from the perspective of the world at large, how we aim to make sure that the benefits of our models exceed their costs.
paraphrase: The RSP sets out how risks are identified, how development and deployment decisions are made, and how benefits are ensured to outweigh costs.

excerpt: We have always intended for our RSP to be a living document.
paraphrase: Anthropic states the RSP has always been intended as a living document.

excerpt: We will continually update the RSP as we learn more about AI capabilities and risks, develop and refine technical safety measures, and gain more experience navigating an ecosystem in which the risks to society depend on the actions of many developers.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to continually updating the RSP as understanding of capabilities, risks, safety measures, and the multi-developer ecosystem grows.

excerpt: The major components of this third iteration are as follows:
paraphrase: This sentence introduces the list of major components of the third RSP iteration.

excerpt: Our recommendations for industry-wide safety outline what it would take, at an industry-wide level, to keep catastrophic risks reliably low through a period of rapid advances in AI capabilities.
paraphrase: The document describes industry-wide recommendations for keeping catastrophic risk low during rapid AI advancement.

excerpt: We lay this out in a table that maps capability thresholds to the mitigations we believe they call for.
paraphrase: A table maps capability thresholds to corresponding mitigations.

excerpt: We also include our planned mitigations as a company, which are drawn from other sections of this policy and associated artifacts.
paraphrase: The table also includes company-specific planned mitigations sourced from other parts of the policy.

excerpt: This approach represents a change from our previous RSP, driven by a collective action problem.
paraphrase: The new approach is explained as a change from the prior RSP due to a collective action problem.

excerpt: The overall level of catastrophic risk from AI depends on the actions of multiple AI developers, not just one.
paraphrase: Catastrophic AI risk depends on the collective actions of multiple developers.

excerpt: Our previous RSP committed to implementing mitigations that would reduce our models' absolute risk levels to acceptable levels, without regard to whether other frontier AI developers would do the same.
paraphrase: The prior RSP committed to reducing absolute risk regardless of other developers' actions.

excerpt: But from a societal perspective, what matters is the risk to the ecosystem as a whole.
paraphrase: From society's viewpoint, the relevant risk is that of the whole ecosystem, not a single developer.

excerpt: If one AI developer paused development to implement safety measures while others moved forward with training and deploying AI systems without strong mitigations, that could result in a world that is less safe—the developers with the weakest protections would set the pace, and responsible developers would lose their ability to do safety research and advance the public benefit.
paraphrase: Unilateral pausing by one developer while others proceed unsafely could make the world less safe overall, ceding pace-setting to the least protective actors.

excerpt: Although this situation has not yet arisen, it looks likely enough that we want to prepare for it.
paraphrase: This collective action problem has not yet materialized but is likely enough to warrant preparation.

excerpt: We now separate our plans as a company—those which we expect to achieve regardless of what any other company does—from our more ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
paraphrase: Anthropic now distinguishes its own company commitments from broader, more ambitious industry-wide recommendations.

excerpt: We aspire to advance the latter through a mixture of example-setting, addressing unsolved technical problems, advocacy through industry groups, and policy advocacy.
paraphrase: Anthropic aims to advance industry-wide recommendations via example-setting, technical work, industry advocacy, and policy advocacy.

excerpt: But we cannot commit to following them unilaterally.
paraphrase: Anthropic states it cannot unilaterally commit to the industry-wide recommendations.

excerpt: Frontier Safety Roadmaps are a new requirement under our RSP.
paraphrase: Frontier Safety Roadmaps are introduced as a new RSP requirement.

excerpt: These will describe our concrete plans for making progress across Security, Alignment, Safeguards, and Policy.
paraphrase: The Roadmaps will detail plans for progress in Security, Alignment, Safeguards, and Policy.

excerpt: Goals described in the Roadmaps are intended to be ambitious, yet achievable—providing the kind of forcing function that we consider to be a past success of our RSP.
paraphrase: Roadmap goals are meant to be ambitious yet achievable, functioning as a forcing mechanism similar to past RSP successes.

excerpt: These are not hard commitments but rather public goals against which we will openly grade our progress.
paraphrase: Roadmap goals are not binding commitments but public benchmarks for openly tracking progress.

excerpt: Risk Reports are another new requirement.
paraphrase: Risk Reports are introduced as another new RSP requirement.

excerpt: Risk Reports will provide detailed information on the safety profile of our models at the time of publication.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will detail the safety profile of models as of publication.

excerpt: They will go beyond describing model capabilities, addressing our thinking on how capabilities, threat models (the specific ways that models might pose threats), and active risk mitigations fit together, providing an assessment of the overall level of risk.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will integrate capabilities, threat models, and mitigations into an overall risk assessment, beyond just describing capabilities.

excerpt: These reports will reflect our reasoning as to whether we believe the risks of training or deploying our models are justified by their corresponding benefits to the world.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will explain whether the risks of training/deploying models are justified by their benefits.

excerpt: They will be published online, with some redactions to protect sensitive details about, for example, our training methods and organizations with whom we work.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published online with redactions to protect sensitive information such as training methods and partner organizations.

excerpt: As detailed below, we also aim to subject Risk Reports to review by credible, independent external parties.
paraphrase: Anthropic aims to have Risk Reports reviewed by credible independent external parties.

excerpt: Finally, our governance commitments are intended to promote internal and external accountability, similar to those in our previous RSP.
paraphrase: Governance commitments continue to aim at internal and external accountability, similar to the prior RSP.

excerpt: Our RSP is only one part of our overall approach to safety.
paraphrase: The RSP is only one component of Anthropic's broader safety approach.

excerpt: For instance, although this policy focuses on catastrophic risks, they are not the only risks we consider important—our Usage Policy and societal impacts research address other concerns.
paraphrase: Other risks beyond catastrophic ones are addressed by the Usage Policy and societal impacts research.

excerpt: Further, the RSP may serve some regulatory requirements, but it is not designed to be comprehensive.
paraphrase: The RSP may partially satisfy regulatory requirements but is not intended to be comprehensive regulatory compliance.

excerpt: We want to keep it focused on our most central measures for addressing the catastrophic risks we prioritize most, rather than expand it to address every obligation we face.
paraphrase: The RSP is deliberately kept focused on core catastrophic-risk measures rather than every obligation.

excerpt: Where regulatory requirements exceed or differ from what the RSP covers, we will address them through separate documents.
paraphrase: Additional or differing regulatory requirements will be handled in separate documents.

excerpt: "Catastrophic risk" as used in our RSP refers generally to risks of the most severe potential harms from advanced AI, such as existential threats or fundamental destabilization of global systems.
paraphrase: Footnote defines catastrophic risk as the most severe potential AI harms, such as existential threats or global destabilization.

excerpt: We use this term in its plain meaning rather than adopting any specific statutory definition.
paraphrase: The term catastrophic risk is used in its plain meaning, not a statutory definition.

excerpt: Where laws such as California SB 53 define this or similar terms with specific thresholds, we address those requirements in separate compliance frameworks.
paraphrase: Statutory definitions such as California SB 53's are handled through separate compliance frameworks.

excerpt: This section outlines our recommendations for what it would take, at an industry-wide level, to keep catastrophic risks reliably low through a period of rapid advances in AI capabilities.
paraphrase: This section presents recommendations for industry-wide measures to keep catastrophic risk low amid rapid AI progress.

excerpt: We lay this out in a three-column table.
paraphrase: The recommendations are presented in a three-column table.

excerpt: The left column identifies capability thresholds that would call for heightened mitigations.
paraphrase: The left column of the table lists capability thresholds requiring heightened mitigations.

excerpt: The middle column provides an overview of our planned mitigations, which we have set forth more fully in our Frontier Safety Roadmap and other sections of this policy.
paraphrase: The middle column summarizes planned mitigations detailed further in the Roadmap and elsewhere in the policy.

excerpt: The right column describes our recommendations for industry-wide safety at each threshold.
paraphrase: The right column contains the industry-wide safety recommendations for each threshold.

excerpt: The distinction between our plans as a company (middle column) and our industry-wide recommendations (right column) reflects the limitations of any single AI developer's ability to ensure safety across the industry.
paraphrase: The company/industry-wide distinction reflects that a single developer cannot ensure industry-wide safety alone.

excerpt: In particular, we cannot unilaterally and unconditionally commit to staying in line with the industry-wide recommendations in the right column.
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot unilaterally and unconditionally commit to the industry-wide recommendations.

excerpt: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
paraphrase: The recommendations will nonetheless shape important aspects of Anthropic's work, as detailed below.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We use these recommendations as the north star for our risk mitigations planning as well as our public policy work.
paraphrase: The recommendations serve as the guiding standard for risk mitigation planning and public policy work.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We will strive to advance these recommendations through a mixture of example-setting, addressing unsolved technical problems, advocacy through industry groups, and policy advocacy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will try to advance these recommendations through example-setting, technical work, industry advocacy, and policy advocacy.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We have also adopted a set of competitor-contingent commitments (see Appendix A) aimed at staying in line with these recommendations in scenarios where we can be confident that other relevant AI developers are doing the same.
paraphrase: Anthropic has adopted competitor-contingent commitments to follow the recommendations when confident other developers do likewise.

excerpt: At this point in AI's rapid development, we cannot presently give highly specific advance detail on what evaluations will determine whether risk thresholds have been passed, or what risk mitigations will be needed to achieve safety.
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot currently specify in detail the evaluations for passing risk thresholds or the mitigations needed.

excerpt: Our recommendations for industry-wide safety are thus structured around requiring analysis and arguments making a strong case for safety, rather than AI Safety Levels (more in Appendix B).
paraphrase: The recommendations rely on requiring safety-case analysis and argument rather than fixed AI Safety Levels.

excerpt: This leaves flexibility in how risk thresholds are evaluated and how safety is achieved and argued for.
paraphrase: This structure allows flexibility in threshold evaluation and safety argumentation.

excerpt: But it creates a challenge: one actor's view of what constitutes good risk assessment and mitigation may be very different from another's.
paraphrase: This flexibility creates a challenge because views on adequate risk assessment and mitigation may differ across actors.

excerpt: Ultimately, the best way for these recommendations to be implemented is likely via governance of all relevant frontier AI developers by third parties that determine which developers need to provide risk analyses and make arguments for the safety of their systems, and determine which such arguments are adequate.
paraphrase: Anthropic suggests third-party governance of all frontier developers as the best implementation path, determining who must provide risk analyses and judging their adequacy.

excerpt: To the extent this takes the form of national regulation, different countries should attempt to harmonize their governance, including standards of evidence, to avoid a race to the bottom.
paraphrase: Countries should harmonize national regulation and evidentiary standards to avoid a race to the bottom.

excerpt: In the shorter run, independent bodies (standards-setting organizations, auditors, etc.) might review such arguments and enforce high quality standards for private AI developers via voluntary mechanisms.
paraphrase: In the near term, independent bodies could voluntarily review and enforce quality standards for private AI developers.

excerpt: Note that an AI developer might provide a single analysis covering a broad category of models, such that there isn't a new analysis needed for each release.
paraphrase: A single analysis could cover a broad model category rather than requiring per-release analyses.

excerpt: Additionally, determinations of which AI developers need to provide such analysis should be made with an effort to spare smaller AI developers from unnecessary compliance burden.
paraphrase: Determinations of which developers must provide analysis should try to spare smaller developers unnecessary compliance burden.

excerpt: We expect that the recommendations for industry-wide safety will evolve significantly, as we learn more about AI capabilities, threat models, and risk mitigations.
paraphrase: The industry-wide recommendations are expected to evolve significantly as knowledge improves.

excerpt: We hope these recommendations will become increasingly specific over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic hopes the recommendations become more specific over time.

excerpt: We will consider this threshold to be met if we determine that either (1) our models would be able to fully substitute for our entire set of Research Scientists and Research Engineers, at competitive costs (i.e., within a factor of 5); or (2) there is "dramatic acceleration" of the pace of AI progress for reasons that likely relate to the automation of AI R&D.
paraphrase: The threshold is met if models could fully replace all Research Scientists/Engineers at competitive cost (within 5x), or if AI-driven R&D automation causes dramatic acceleration.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.

paraphrase: Scenario (2) requires observing double the expected AI capability progress rate attributable substantially to R&D automation rather than other factors, with potential for further acceleration.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:

paraphrase: Recommended argument: no user or team, even state-backed, gains significantly increased ability to cause catastrophic harm via product use or weight theft.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: This will likely require similar measures to those listed in row 1, but to a higher standard‚ to the point where even well-resourced and -staffed threat actors would be unlikely to reliably jailbreak models or cause catastrophic harm via unauthorized access to or modification of models (including via stolen or modified model weights).
paraphrase: This requires row-1-type measures at a higher standard sufficient to resist well-resourced threat actors from jailbreaking or misusing stolen/modified weights.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: Accomplishing this would likely mean security roughly in line with RAND SL4. Security requirements would be calibrated to defend against the strongest plausible threat actors who are not bound by a credible industry-wide safety regime.
paraphrase: This implies security roughly at RAND SL4, calibrated against the strongest plausible unbound threat actors.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 1
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:

paraphrase: Developers under a credible industry-wide regime would not need to treat each other as weight-theft threats.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: Even malicious employees and other insiders with maximal levels of access will not be significantly enabled to cause catastrophic harm.
paraphrase: Recommended argument: even maximally privileged malicious insiders would not be significantly enabled to cause catastrophic harm.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:

paraphrase: This requires accounting for less-restricted internal tools and the possibility of unauthorized model modification.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:

paraphrase: This likely requires an internal Usage Policy plus strong compartmentalization/controls/monitoring restricting even the CEO and top technical staff from circumventing it.

context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: AI models have not been deliberately or inadvertently trained with dangerous goals, or are otherwise unlikely to autonomously cause catastrophic harm.
paraphrase: Recommended argument: models have not been trained (deliberately or inadvertently) with dangerous goals and are unlikely to autonomously cause catastrophic harm.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 3
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: This will likely require similar measures to those listed above under "High-stakes sabotage opportunities" (some combination of internal compartmentalization, restriction and code review; monitoring AI behavior; and evidence that AI models lack the propensity to deceive and manipulate users), but to a greater degree.
paraphrase: This requires similar but stronger measures to those under high-stakes sabotage: compartmentalization, monitoring, and evidence against deceptive/manipulative propensities.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 3
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: In particular, at this point AI systems might be responsible for much of the research and analysis that underpins risk assessment, and might have strong capabilities for deception, manipulation and obfuscation of evidence, in which case analyses of threats from AIs should follow very high evidentiary standards with thorough and careful analysis of the possibility that much of the key evidence is suspect due to the possibility of manipulation by AI systems.
paraphrase: Because AI may generate much of the risk-assessment evidence and could be capable of deception/manipulation, threat analyses should apply very high evidentiary standards accounting for possible evidence manipulation.

excerpt: We will maintain a Frontier Safety Roadmap laying out ambitious but achievable goals for improving our risk mitigations—charting our progress as a company and raising the bar over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a Frontier Safety Roadmap with ambitious, achievable goals that track and raise the bar on risk mitigation progress.

excerpt: Maintaining and reporting on this Roadmap is part of our work under the RSP.
paraphrase: Roadmap maintenance and reporting are part of the RSP's obligations.

excerpt: It will be shared with all full-time employees as well as our Board of Directors (Board) and Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT), and published in redacted form.
paraphrase: The Roadmap will be shared internally with all full-time employees, the Board, and the LTBT, and published externally in redacted form.

excerpt: We will provide updates on whether we achieve the goals, and set new goals when we do.
paraphrase: Anthropic will report on goal achievement and set new goals as achieved.

excerpt: Our Frontier Safety Roadmap is subject to change.
paraphrase: The Roadmap can change over time.

excerpt: Some changes may simply reflect our evolving understanding of how best to mitigate key risks.
paraphrase: Changes to the Roadmap may reflect evolving understanding of risk mitigation.

excerpt: However, we will strive to avoid situations where we revise the goals in a less ambitious direction simply because we are unable to achieve them.
paraphrase: Anthropic will try to avoid weakening Roadmap goals merely due to an inability to meet them.

excerpt: By establishing this expectation, we hope to create a forcing function for work that would otherwise be challenging to appropriately prioritize and resource, as it requires collaboration (and in some cases sacrifices) from multiple parts of the company and can be at cross-purposes with immediate competitive and commercial priorities.
paraphrase: This expectation is meant to force prioritization of cross-company collaborative work that might otherwise conflict with competitive/commercial priorities.

excerpt: Publishing our Frontier Safety Roadmap may also help inform broader industry and policy discussions on AI safety.
paraphrase: Publishing the Roadmap may also contribute to broader industry and policy discussions on AI safety.

excerpt: Our current Frontier Safety Roadmap is available at anthropic.com/responsible-scaling-policy/roadmap.
paraphrase: The current Roadmap is published at a specified Anthropic URL.

excerpt: We will also keep past Roadmaps available at that link.
paraphrase: Past versions of the Roadmap will remain accessible at the same link.

excerpt: We will publish Risk Reports discussing the risks of our systems and how we have made determinations about whether to continue AI development and deployment in light of the risks.
paraphrase: Anthropic will publish Risk Reports that discuss system risks and the determinations made about continuing development and deployment.

excerpt: These have significant content in common with system cards, but we are adding additional structure and process aimed at presenting our overall assessments of risk.
paraphrase: Risk Reports overlap substantially with system cards but add structure and process for presenting overall risk assessments.

excerpt: Scope. A Risk Report will cover all publicly deployed models at the time of its publication.
paraphrase: A Risk Report's scope includes all models publicly deployed at the time of publication.

excerpt: It will also cover internally deployed models when we determine that these models could pose significant risks5 beyond those posed by models that are covered by a prior Risk Report.
paraphrase: Internally deployed models are also covered if determined to pose significant risks beyond previously covered models.

excerpt: While there are a variety of reasons we might classify an internal model this way, this will—at a minimum—include any internal models that we are deploying for large-scale, fully autonomous research.
paraphrase: At minimum, internal models used for large-scale, fully autonomous research will be classified as posing significant risk.

excerpt: Models fitting the above description are abbreviated below as "in-scope models."
paraphrase: Models meeting the scope description are termed "in-scope models."

excerpt: We may also voluntarily include additional models in a Risk Report, e.g., to contribute to general discourse, but such inclusion does not expand the commitments below.
paraphrase: Additional models may be voluntarily included for discourse purposes without expanding the stated commitments.

excerpt: Timing. We will publish a Risk Report every 3-6 months.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published on a 3-6 month cadence.

excerpt: Note that unlike system cards, Risk Reports will not be published with each new model release.
paraphrase: Risk Reports differ from system cards in that they are not tied to every model release.

excerpt: When we publicly deploy a model that we determine is significantly more capable than any of the models covered in the most recent Risk Report, we will publish a discussion (in our System Card or elsewhere) of how that model's capabilities and propensities affect or change the analysis in the Risk Report.
paraphrase: If a newly deployed public model is significantly more capable than those in the latest Risk Report, a discussion of its impact on the analysis will be published.

excerpt: Within 30 days of determining that we have an internally deployed model that is in-scope (per the description above), we will publish a discussion (in a System Card or elsewhere) of how that model's capabilities and propensities affect or change the analysis in the Risk Report.
paraphrase: Within 30 days of identifying an in-scope internally deployed model, a discussion of its effect on the Risk Report analysis will be published.

excerpt: Specifically, risks arising from the capability thresholds in our recommendations for industry-wide safety (see Section 1).
paraphrase: Footnote clarifies that significant risks refer to those from capability thresholds in the industry-wide safety recommendations.

excerpt: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
paraphrase: The section introduces guiding principles for Risk Reports.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We intend for our Risk Reports to be direct, candid, and informative about how we see the risks of our systems and our state of preparedness for them.
paraphrase: Risk Reports are intended to be direct, candid, and informative about system risks and preparedness.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: In particular, we will acknowledge when we view certain models as posing significant risks in absolute terms, even if our marginal contribution to overall ecosystem risk may be relatively limited when taking other developers' AI models into account.
paraphrase: Anthropic will acknowledge significant absolute risk of its models even if its marginal contribution to ecosystem risk is limited.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: We will put significant effort into investigating (for example, via capability evaluations) the case for risk, and into sharing what we find.
paraphrase: Significant effort will be devoted to investigating risk cases, such as through capability evaluations, and to sharing findings.

context_stem: Several principles guide how we approach Risk Reports:
excerpt: When a Risk Report describes risk mitigations we have in place (or plan to implement shortly), we will keep our future practices in line with this description or track and report noteworthy changes and deviations (generally via subsequent Risk Reports).
paraphrase: Future practices will remain consistent with described mitigations, or noteworthy changes will be tracked and reported in later Risk Reports.

context_stem: When a Risk Report describes risk mitigations we have in place...
excerpt: We should make a strong attempt to ensure that ongoing (as opposed to temporary) changes do not significantly increase the level of risk.
paraphrase: A strong effort should be made to ensure ongoing changes do not significantly raise risk levels.

excerpt: Factual information. We will describe how we identify, evaluate, and mitigate catastrophic risks.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will describe processes for identifying, evaluating, and mitigating catastrophic risks.

excerpt: A Risk Report will document the following:
paraphrase: The Risk Report will document a list of items.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Threat model identification: Our criteria for determining which catastrophic risks (i.e., threat models) we assess.
paraphrase: The report will document criteria used to determine which catastrophic risk threat models are assessed.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Threat model specification: The relevant threat models (which will, at a minimum, include those discussed above).
paraphrase: The report will specify relevant threat models, including at minimum those previously discussed.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Evidence (including evaluations) about relevant model capabilities and behaviors: For each in-scope model, capability and alignment evaluations (conducted internally and by external parties as appropriate), their results, and (as appropriate) other evidence we considered in assessing the level of risk.
paraphrase: For each in-scope model, the report will document capability and alignment evaluation evidence, results, and other risk-relevant evidence.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Risk mitigations: For each in-scope model, the mitigations we are implementing across security, deployment safeguards, and alignment domains, along with discussion of their effectiveness.
paraphrase: For each in-scope model, the report documents mitigations across security, deployment safeguards, and alignment and their effectiveness.

context_stem: A Risk Report will document the following:
excerpt: Additional relevant factors: Any other considerations material to our risk analysis.
paraphrase: The report will include any other considerations material to the risk analysis.

excerpt: Risk analyses. We will provide our reasoning and conclusions regarding both specific threat models and overall risk levels.
paraphrase: Risk analyses will present reasoning and conclusions about specific threat models and overall risk levels.

excerpt: Our analyses will include:
paraphrase: The analyses will include the following items.

excerpt: Threat-specific risk assessment: For each threat model, we will analyze remaining absolute risk–i.e., the leftover risk after accounting for our mitigations.
paraphrase: For each threat model, remaining absolute risk after mitigations will be analyzed.

context_stem: Our analyses will include: Threat-specific risk assessment...
excerpt: We will also discuss whether we believe we've crossed relevant thresholds in our recommendations for industry-wide safety (see Section 1), and (as relevant) whether we believe we're meeting the risk mitigation standards corresponding to them.
paraphrase: The report will discuss whether relevant safety thresholds have been crossed and whether corresponding mitigation standards are being met.

excerpt: Overall risk assessment: We will provide an overall risk assessment.
paraphrase: An overall risk assessment will be provided.

excerpt: Risk-benefit determination: We will explain whether, and if so why, we believe the identified risks are justified by corresponding benefits.
paraphrase: The report will explain whether and why identified risks are justified by corresponding benefits.

excerpt: Looking forward: We will outline our plans for continuing to monitor and mitigate the relevant risks over time.
paraphrase: Plans for ongoing monitoring and mitigation of relevant risks will be outlined.

excerpt: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
paraphrase: This part of the report addresses review of past Risk Reports and decisions.

context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
excerpt: Changes in risk mitigation practices—noteworthy cases in which our risk mitigation practices deviated (including temporarily) or changed from what we discussed in our previous Risk Report over the relevant period, and their implications for the overall level of risk.
paraphrase: The report addresses noteworthy deviations or changes in risk mitigation practices since the last Risk Report and their implications for overall risk.

context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
excerpt: Decisions to internally deploy in-scope models that would not otherwise be reviewed in a Risk Report (because they happened in between Risk Reports).
paraphrase: The report covers internal deployment decisions of in-scope models that occurred between Risk Reports.

context_stem: Decisions to internally deploy in-scope models...
excerpt: We will discuss how these decisions were made and whether they appear reasonable in light of any noteworthy new information that has come to light since then.
paraphrase: The report will discuss how such deployment decisions were made and whether they were reasonable given subsequent new information.

context_stem: Review of past Risk Reports and decisions. We will address:
excerpt: Changes to our Frontier Safety Roadmap and any cases where we failed to meet our goals.
paraphrase: The report addresses changes to the Frontier Safety Roadmap and instances of unmet goals.

excerpt: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis. If we determine that the absolute level of risk being imposed industry-wide by AI systems such as ours is high, and are justifying our decision to move forward based partly on a marginal risk analysis,6 we will additionally address the following:
paraphrase: If industry-wide absolute risk is determined high and the decision to proceed partly relies on marginal risk analysis, additional items will be addressed.

context_stem: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis... we will additionally address the following:
excerpt: Competitive landscape analysis: What we know about how our current and future model capabilities and risk mitigations compare to those of relevant competitors.
paraphrase: The additional analysis compares current and future model capabilities and mitigations to competitors.

context_stem: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis... we will additionally address the following:
excerpt: Role in risk assessment: How these comparisons factored into our risk assessment.
paraphrase: The analysis explains how competitive comparisons factored into the risk assessment.

context_stem: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis... we will additionally address the following:
excerpt: Benefits analysis: The benefits, if any, of continuing to maintain our existing models or of advancing frontier capabilities, including considerations related to our mission and our ability to contribute to AI safety research and policy development.
paraphrase: The analysis includes benefits of maintaining models or advancing capabilities, including mission-related considerations and safety research contributions.

context_stem: Marginal risk and ecosystem analysis... we will additionally address the following:
excerpt: Advocacy efforts: The steps we took to raise public awareness of the relevant risks and to encourage appropriate regulatory action, including our engagement with policymakers and other AI developers.
paraphrase: The analysis documents steps taken to raise public awareness of risks and encourage regulatory action, including policymaker engagement.

excerpt: We will conduct the assessments above with respect to each in-scope model.
paraphrase: All the described assessments will be conducted for each in-scope model.

excerpt: To avoid redundancy, we will likely analyze similar models collectively rather than individually, with appropriate justification for any such groupings.
paraphrase: Similar models may be analyzed collectively rather than individually, with justification, to avoid redundancy.

excerpt: Initial assessment and drafting: Our internal subject matter experts will conduct risk assessments and draft the Risk Report.
paraphrase: Internal subject matter experts conduct the risk assessments and draft the Risk Report.

excerpt: Review and feedback: We will solicit comprehensive internal feedback on the report, focusing on identifying potential methodological weaknesses, analytical gaps, or areas requiring additional evidence or clarification.
paraphrase: Comprehensive internal feedback will be sought to identify methodological weaknesses, gaps, or areas needing more evidence.

excerpt: We may also use this feedback to improve or refine the report itself.
paraphrase: Feedback may also be used to improve or refine the report.

excerpt: We will usually also seek feedback from trusted external parties with relevant expertise.
paraphrase: Feedback from trusted external experts will usually also be sought.

excerpt: Executive approval: The Risk Report, along with the internal feedback and any available external feedback, will be sent to the CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer (RSO) for final review and approval.
paraphrase: The Risk Report and associated feedback are sent to the CEO and RSO for final review and approval.

excerpt: The CEO and RSO will make the ultimate determination regarding the adequacy of the risk assessment and any downstream deployment or development plans.
paraphrase: The CEO and RSO make the final determination on the adequacy of the risk assessment and related deployment or development plans.

excerpt: Governance notification: Following approval of a Risk Report, the CEO and RSO will promptly share their decision(s), the underlying Risk Report, and internal feedback with both the Board and the LTBT.
paraphrase: After approval, the CEO and RSO promptly share the decision, Risk Report, and internal feedback with the Board and the LTBT.

excerpt: Modified process when marginal risk analysis is important to our case. In the event that marginal risk analysis (see previous section) plays a major role in a decision to move forward, explicit approval of the Risk Report by the Board and LTBT (rather than just the CEO and RSO) will be required.
paraphrase: If marginal risk analysis plays a major role in a decision to proceed, explicit Board and LTBT approval is required instead of just CEO and RSO approval.

excerpt: By "marginal risk analysis," we mean arguing that the risks imposed by our systems in particular are relatively lower when keeping in mind the risks unavoidably posed by other AI systems.
paraphrase: Footnote defines marginal risk analysis as an argument that a system's risks are relatively lower given unavoidable risks from other AI systems.

excerpt: We will publish a public version of our Risk Report.
paraphrase: A public version of the Risk Report will be published.

excerpt: We will aim to minimize redactions to the public version of the report.
paraphrase: The aim is to minimize redactions in the public version of the report.

excerpt: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
paraphrase: A non-exhaustive list of reasons for redaction follows.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Legal compliance: To comply with legal obligations on disclosing information, such as export control regulations, national security restrictions, or contractual obligations with third parties.
paraphrase: Redaction may occur to comply with legal disclosure obligations such as export controls, national security, or contractual duties.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Intellectual property protection: To protect proprietary information, including technical details of our models and training methodologies, trade secrets, or other confidential business information.
paraphrase: Redaction may protect proprietary information such as technical model details, training methods, or trade secrets.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Public safety considerations: To protect public safety by not disclosing information that could be exploited to cause harm.
paraphrase: Redaction may protect public safety by withholding information that could enable harm.

context_stem: Reasons we may redact material include but are not limited to:
excerpt: Privacy: To protect the personal privacy of individuals.
paraphrase: Redaction may protect individuals' personal privacy.

excerpt: We will work toward a practice of seeking comprehensive, public external review on our Risk Reports.
paraphrase: Anthropic will work toward comprehensive, public external review of its Risk Reports.

excerpt: This means working with one or more third-party organizations that will receive private versions of our Risk Reports (unredacted or with minimal redactions, as discussed below) and publish comprehensive commentary on them.
paraphrase: Third-party organizations will receive private, largely unredacted versions of Risk Reports and publish comprehensive commentary.

excerpt: Commentary will address topics including the quality of our reasoning, the validity of our risk assessments, the overall level of risk, and whether the redactions we've made for the public version are reasonable and appropriate.
paraphrase: External commentary will cover reasoning quality, risk assessment validity, overall risk level, and reasonableness of redactions.

excerpt: Our intent is for external reviewers' judgments to carry significant weight in the eyes of the public as well as our employees.
paraphrase: External reviewer judgments are intended to carry significant weight with both the public and employees.

excerpt: But there are no well-established organizations or procedures for this sort of practice, and we are approaching it as an experiment.
paraphrase: Because no well-established organizations or procedures exist for this practice, it is being approached experimentally.

excerpt: At a minimum, we will complete a full external review process (described below) with at least one external reviewer anytime a Risk Report covers highly capable models and is significantly redacted, defined as follows:
paraphrase: A full external review process with at least one reviewer will be completed whenever a Risk Report covers highly capable models and is significantly redacted, as defined below.

excerpt: A model is "highly capable" if we conclude that it crosses the threshold for automated AI R&D described in Section 1.
paraphrase: A model is deemed highly capable if it crosses the automated AI R&D threshold described in Section 1.

excerpt: "Significantly redacted" means that the redactions omit information a reasonable external safety researcher would consider important in evaluating the overall level of risk, such that a reader of only the public version could not meaningfully assess whether they agree with our conclusions.
paraphrase: Significantly redacted means redactions omit information important to evaluating risk, such that a public-only reader could not meaningfully assess agreement with conclusions.

excerpt: A report shall be deemed significantly redacted if, in the judgment of the RSO, CEO, Board, or LTBT, it meets this description.
paraphrase: A report is deemed significantly redacted if the RSO, CEO, Board, or LTBT judge it meets that description.

excerpt: Note that unredacted reports will be shared with a large number of employees, who will be in a position to raise concerns if they believe the public version meets this description.
paraphrase: Unredacted reports will be shared with many employees, who can raise concerns if they believe the public version is significantly redacted.

excerpt: In addition, upon the LTBT's request, we will conduct a public or private external review of our Risk Report or sections thereof, subject to the procedures outlined below.
paraphrase: At the LTBT's request, a public or private external review of the Risk Report or parts of it will be conducted per the outlined procedures.

excerpt: We will select external reviewers that:
paraphrase: The following criteria guide the selection of external reviewers.

context_stem: We will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: Have significant experience and expertise regarding evaluations for dangerous AI capabilities and propensities.
paraphrase: Reviewers must have significant experience and expertise in evaluating dangerous AI capabilities and propensities.

excerpt: It's particularly important that they be knowledgeable about potential ways such evaluations might be misleading (for example, alignment faking).
paraphrase: Reviewers should particularly understand ways such evaluations could be misleading, such as alignment faking.

context_stem: We will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: Have reputational and other incentives making them likely to be candid about their assessment of risks, rather than focused on writing comments that Anthropic will approve of.
paraphrase: Reviewers should have incentives to be candid about risk assessments rather than to please Anthropic.

excerpt: For example, external review parties should not be teams whose revenue, reputation and success depend entirely on Anthropic and similar companies continuing to work with them.
paraphrase: External reviewers should not be entirely dependent on Anthropic and similar companies for revenue, reputation, or success.

context_stem: We will select external reviewers that:
excerpt: Do not have conflicts of interest with respect to Anthropic.
paraphrase: Reviewers must not have conflicts of interest regarding Anthropic.

context_stem: Do not have conflicts of interest with respect to Anthropic.
excerpt: At a minimum, a reviewing organization itself may not have a financial interest in Anthropic; and the individuals involved in conducting the review, as well as anyone above them in the reporting chain within their organization, may not have a financial interest in Anthropic or close personal relationships with anyone at Anthropic (i.e., family relationships, romantic relationships, or shared living arrangements).
paraphrase: Neither the reviewing organization nor individuals conducting or overseeing the review may hold financial interests in Anthropic or close personal relationships with Anthropic staff.

excerpt: In selecting external reviewers, we will consult with the Board and obtain the approval of the LTBT.
paraphrase: The Board will be consulted and LTBT approval obtained in selecting external reviewers.

excerpt: The external review process will involve sharing the Risk Report with one or more external reviewers within one week of submitting the same report to our Board and LTBT.
paraphrase: External reviewers receive the Risk Report within one week of its submission to the Board and LTBT.

excerpt: We will ask the external reviewers to provide public commentary on our report within 30 days of receipt.
paraphrase: External reviewers are asked to provide public commentary within 30 days of receiving the report.

excerpt: We will try to work toward a process that involves the full external review being completed prior to Board/LTBT review (and may require this later).
paraphrase: Efforts will be made toward completing full external review before Board/LTBT review, potentially becoming a requirement later.

excerpt: For purposes of external review, the only redactions to the Risk Report will be those necessary to comply with legal prohibitions or to maintain our legal rights.7
paraphrase: For external review purposes, redactions are limited to those legally necessary or needed to preserve legal rights.

excerpt: We expect that we will also invest some time in answering follow-up questions from parties doing external review.
paraphrase: Time will also likely be spent answering follow-up questions from external reviewers.

excerpt: The external review will address:
paraphrase: The external review will cover the following topics.

excerpt: Adequacy of information: Whether the Risk Report contains sufficient information to assess the identified risks;
paraphrase: The review assesses whether the Risk Report contains sufficient information to evaluate identified risks.

excerpt: Analytical rigor: The strength of the Risk Report's reasoning and analysis;
paraphrase: The review evaluates the strength of the Risk Report's reasoning and analysis.

excerpt: Areas of disagreement: Whether the external reviewer disagrees with any of the Risk Report's key claims and, if so, the reasons for any such disagreements; and
paraphrase: The review notes whether the reviewer disagrees with key claims and, if so, why.

excerpt: Risk reduction recommendations: Recommendations for further reducing identified risks.
paraphrase: The review provides recommendations for further reducing identified risks.

excerpt: The external reviewer will also evaluate our redaction decisions while avoiding disclosure of the redacted content itself.
paraphrase: The reviewer will also evaluate redaction decisions without disclosing the redacted content.

excerpt: In particular, the review will cover:
paraphrase: The review will specifically cover the following redaction-related items.

context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Redaction scope: The general nature and scope of redactions;
paraphrase: The review covers the general nature and scope of redactions.

context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Redaction justification: Whether the external reviewer generally agrees or disagrees with the publicly stated reasons for the redactions and, if relevant, the reasons for any disagreements;
paraphrase: The review addresses whether the reviewer agrees or disagrees with the stated redaction reasons and why.

context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Balancing test: Whether the redactions strike a reasonable balance between Anthropic's legitimate interests and society's interest in transparency; and
paraphrase: The review assesses whether redactions reasonably balance Anthropic's interests against societal transparency interests.

context_stem: In particular, the review will cover:
excerpt: Materiality: Whether any of the redactions in the public report are material to any of the external reviewer's substantive disagreements with the report's claims.
paraphrase: The review considers whether redactions are material to the reviewer's substantive disagreements with the report's claims.

excerpt: For example, we may redact information if sharing it would endanger our legal right to treat it as confidential. This would be an uncommon situation.
paraphrase: Footnote gives an example: redaction may occur if disclosure would jeopardize a legal right to confidentiality, an uncommon case.

excerpt: It does not mean we would redact information merely because it is sensitive or to reduce the risk of a leak.
paraphrase: Footnote clarifies redaction is not justified merely by sensitivity or leak-risk reduction.

excerpt: Public comments. We will ask the external reviewer to memorialize its findings on the topics above in a written report that is made public.
paraphrase: External reviewers will be asked to document their findings in a written public report.

excerpt: External reviewers will be bound by obligations not to disclose confidential information (e.g., confidential intellectual property, matters of national security, or proprietary details such as model architecture, cost, or size), but beyond that will not be restricted in what they can publish, including concerns about the Risk Report or Anthropic's conduct in connection with the external review.
paraphrase: Reviewers must not disclose specified confidential information but are otherwise unrestricted in publishing, including concerns about the report or Anthropic's conduct.

excerpt: We commit to the following governance measures to promote internal and external accountability.
paraphrase: This section introduces governance measures intended to promote internal and external accountability.

excerpt: Responsible Scaling Officer: We will maintain the position of RSO, a designated member of staff who is responsible for the implementation of this policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a Responsible Scaling Officer role responsible for implementing the policy.

context_stem: The RSO's duties will include (but are not limited to):
excerpt: as needed, proposing updates to this policy;
paraphrase: One RSO duty is proposing policy updates as needed.

context_stem: The RSO's duties will include (but are not limited to):
excerpt: approving relevant model development or deployment decisions based on our risk assessments;
paraphrase: The RSO approves model development or deployment decisions based on risk assessments.

context_stem: The RSO's duties will include (but are not limited to):
excerpt: reviewing major contracts (e.g., deployment partnerships) for consistency with this policy;
paraphrase: The RSO reviews major contracts such as deployment partnerships for policy consistency.

context_stem: The RSO's duties will include (but are not limited to):
excerpt: overseeing the implementation of this policy, including the allocation of sufficient resources;
paraphrase: The RSO oversees policy implementation, including ensuring sufficient resource allocation.

context_stem: The RSO's duties will include (but are not limited to):
excerpt: receiving and addressing reports of potential instances of noncompliance; and
paraphrase: The RSO receives and addresses reports of potential noncompliance.

context_stem: The RSO's duties will include (but are not limited to):
excerpt: making judgment calls on policy interpretation and application.
paraphrase: The RSO makes judgment calls regarding policy interpretation and application.

excerpt: Long Term Benefit Trust: We will regularly brief the LTBT on plans and developments related to our Risk Reports, including model training, capability evals, mitigations, and risk analyses.
paraphrase: Anthropic will regularly update the Long Term Benefit Trust on Risk Report-related plans and developments.

excerpt: Internal transparency: We will share final, unredacted Risk Reports with Anthropic's regular-clearance staff.
paraphrase: Anthropic will share complete, unredacted Risk Reports with regular-clearance staff.

excerpt: Noncompliance reporting: We will maintain a process for Anthropic staff to submit anonymous or identified reports regarding potential noncompliance with this policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a process allowing staff to submit anonymous or identified noncompliance reports.

excerpt: Staff will have more than one option for who receives these reports, including the RSO, and at least one executive who does not report to the RSO.
paraphrase: Staff have multiple reporting recipient options, including the RSO and an executive independent of the RSO.

excerpt: When we receive a report, we will promptly investigate, take appropriate and proportional corrective action if it is substantiated, and document the report and our findings.
paraphrase: Received reports will be promptly investigated, corrective action taken if substantiated, and findings documented.

excerpt: We will provide quarterly updates to the Board regarding reports of potential noncompliance, whether substantiated or not.
paraphrase: The Board receives quarterly updates on noncompliance reports regardless of substantiation status.

excerpt: If we determine that a report is (1) substantiated and (2) involves a material safety risk, we will promptly notify the Board and we may provide public notice of the same.
paraphrase: Substantiated reports involving material safety risk trigger prompt Board notification and possible public disclosure.

excerpt: Finally, we will protect reporters from retaliation, and where a report concerns the conduct of the RSO, at least one recipient will be a member of the Board.
paraphrase: Reporters are protected from retaliation, and reports about the RSO must include a Board member as a recipient.

excerpt: Employee agreements: We will not impose contractual non-disparagement obligations on employees, candidates, or former employees in a way that could impede or discourage them from publicly raising safety concerns about Anthropic.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits not to use non-disparagement clauses that would discourage employees from raising safety concerns.

excerpt: If we offer agreements with a non-disparagement clause, that clause will not preclude raising safety concerns, nor will it preclude disclosure of the existence of that clause.
paraphrase: Any non-disparagement clause used will permit both raising safety concerns and disclosing the clause's existence.

excerpt: Internal review: We will regularly conduct an internal review of our implementation of this policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will regularly review internally how it implements this policy.

excerpt: Procedural compliance review: On approximately an annual basis, we will commission a third-party review that assesses whether we adhered to this policy's main procedural commitments.
paraphrase: Anthropic will commission an annual third-party review of adherence to the policy's procedural commitments.

excerpt: This review will focus on procedural compliance, not substantive outcomes.
paraphrase: The review examines procedural adherence rather than substantive outcomes.

excerpt: Policy changes: Changes to the RSP will be proposed by the CEO and RSO, and approved by the Board in consultation with the LTBT.
paraphrase: RSP changes are proposed by the CEO and RSO and approved by the Board with LTBT consultation.

excerpt: If we update the RSP, we will publicly share the updated version prior to or on its effective date and will record the differences from the prior draft in the Change Log.
paraphrase: RSP updates will be published by their effective date, with changes recorded in the Change Log.

excerpt: We will maintain the current version of the RSP on our website.
paraphrase: The current RSP version is kept publicly available on Anthropic's website.

excerpt: RSP-2023 (aka RSP v1.0): Initial version.
paraphrase: The first changelog entry notes RSP-2023 as the initial version.

excerpt: RSP-2024: This update introduces a more flexible and nuanced approach to assessing and managing AI risks while maintaining our commitment not to train or deploy models unless we have implemented adequate safeguards.
paraphrase: The 2024 update adds a more flexible risk-management approach while retaining the commitment to adequate safeguards before training or deployment.

excerpt: Key improvements include new capability thresholds to indicate when we should upgrade our safeguards, refined processes for evaluating model capabilities and the adequacy of our safeguards (inspired by safety case methodologies), and new measures for internal governance and external input.
paraphrase: Key improvements included new capability thresholds, refined evaluation processes inspired by safety cases, and new governance/external input measures.

excerpt: We describe the most notable changes below.
paraphrase: The notable changes are described in the following entries.

excerpt: ASL definition changed: The term "ASL" now refers to groups of technical and operational safeguards (it previously also referred to models).
paraphrase: The ASL term was redefined to refer only to safeguard groupings rather than also to models.

excerpt: We also introduced the new concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards. This change allows for more targeted application of safeguards based on specific capabilities, rather than broad model categories.
paraphrase: New concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards were introduced, enabling more targeted safeguard application.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: ARA threshold now a checkpoint: We replaced our previous autonomous replication and adaption (ARA) threshold with a "checkpoint" for autonomous AI capabilities.
paraphrase: The prior ARA threshold was replaced with a checkpoint concept for autonomous AI capabilities.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: Rather than triggering higher safety standards automatically, reaching this checkpoint will prompt additional evaluation of the model's capabilities and accelerate our preparation of stronger safeguards.
paraphrase: Reaching the checkpoint prompts further evaluation and accelerated safeguard preparation rather than automatic escalation.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: We previously considered these capabilities as a trigger for increased safeguards, motivated by an attempt to establish some threshold while we developed a better sense of potential threats.
paraphrase: These capabilities were previously used as a safeguard trigger while understanding of threats was still developing.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: We now believe that these capabilities - at the levels we initially considered - would not necessitate the ASL-3 standard.
paraphrase: Anthropic now believes the originally considered capability levels do not require the ASL-3 standard.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / AI R&D threshold added
excerpt: AI R&D threshold added: We added a new threshold for AI systems that can significantly advance AI development.
paraphrase: A new threshold was added for AI systems capable of significantly advancing AI development.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / AI R&D threshold added
excerpt: Such capabilities could lead to rapid, unpredictable advances in AI, potentially outpacing our ability to evaluate and address emerging risks, and may also serve as an early warning sign for the ability to automate R&D in other domains.
paraphrase: These capabilities risk rapid unpredictable AI advances outpacing risk evaluation and could signal broader R&D automation ability.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
excerpt: Testing for Capability Thresholds: Rather than using prespecified evaluations, we now require an affirmative case that models are sufficiently far from Capability Thresholds.
paraphrase: Instead of prespecified evaluations, an affirmative case is now required showing models are sufficiently distant from Capability Thresholds.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
excerpt: Predefined tests may miss emerging risks or be overly conservative relative to the actual threshold of concern.
paraphrase: Predefined tests risk missing emerging risks or being overly conservative relative to the true threshold.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / Testing for Capability Thresholds
excerpt: Our most accurate tests change frequently enough that it is more practical to use this new approach than to have our Board pre-approve evaluations.
paraphrase: Because accurate tests change often, the new approach is more practical than requiring Board pre-approval of evaluations.

excerpt: Adjusted evaluation cadence: We adjusted the comprehensive assessment cadence to 4x Effective Compute or six months of accumulated post-training enhancements (this was previously three months).
paraphrase: The comprehensive assessment cadence changed to 4x Effective Compute or six months of post-training enhancements, up from three months.
stated_bar: 4x Effective Compute or six months (previously three months)

excerpt: We found that a three-month cadence forced teams to prioritize conducting frequent evaluations over more comprehensive testing and improving methodologies.
paraphrase: The prior three-month cadence pushed teams toward frequent evaluation at the expense of comprehensive testing and methodology improvement.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: Less prescriptive evaluation methodology: We have replaced some specifics in our previous testing methodology (e.g., using 1% of compute for elicitation or creating a 6x buffer), with more general requirements to (a) match expected efforts of potential adversaries and (b) provide informal estimates of how further scaling and research developments will impact model capabilities and performance on the same tasks.
paraphrase: Specific prior methodology details (like 1% compute for elicitation or a 6x buffer) were replaced with general requirements to match adversary effort and estimate scaling impacts.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: We have found that specific methodologies may become outdated when new research developments are introduced.
paraphrase: Specific methodologies risk becoming outdated as new research emerges.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology
excerpt: Although still an aspirational goal, the science of evaluations is not currently mature enough to make confident predictions about the precise buffer we should require between current models and a Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: Precise buffer prediction between current models and a Capability Threshold remains an aspirational goal given the immature science of evaluations.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
excerpt: More outcome-focused safeguard requirements: We have updated our ASL-3 safeguards requirements to be less prescriptive and more outcome-focused.
paraphrase: ASL-3 safeguard requirements were updated to be more outcome-focused and less prescriptive.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
excerpt: Rather than detailing specific operational and technical safeguards, we now specify the overall security or deployment standards and requirements for meeting them.
paraphrase: Instead of detailed specific safeguards, overall security or deployment standards and their requirements are now specified.

locator: Changelog / v2.0 / More outcome-focused safeguard requirements
excerpt: This is to allow us to adapt our safeguards more flexibly as our understanding of risks and possible safeguards improves.
paraphrase: The change allows more flexible safeguard adaptation as understanding of risk and mitigations improves.

paraphrase: The update clarifies which actors are covered by the ASL-3 Security Standard.

paraphrase: The v2.1 update clarifies which Capability Thresholds require safeguards beyond current ASL-3 standards.

paraphrase: A new CBRN-related capability threshold was added, defining capabilities that could substantially uplift moderately resourced state programs.

excerpt: We have also disaggregated our existing AI R&D capability thresholds, separating them into two distinct levels (the ability to fully automate entry-level AI research work, and the ability to cause dramatic acceleration in the rate of effective scaling) and provided additional detail on the corresponding Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: AI R&D capability thresholds were split into two levels—full automation of entry-level research and dramatic scaling acceleration—with more detail on corresponding Required Safeguards.

paraphrase: Anthropic committed to reevaluating Capability Thresholds each time Required Safeguards are upgraded.

excerpt: We have decided not to maintain a commitment to define ASL-N+1 evaluations by the time we develop ASL-N models; such an approach would add unnecessary complexity because Capability Thresholds do not naturally come grouped in discrete levels.
paraphrase: The commitment to define ASL-N+1 evaluations by the time ASL-N models are developed was dropped as unnecessarily complex given Capability Thresholds aren't naturally discrete.

excerpt: We believe it is more practical and sensible instead to commit to reconsidering the whole list of Capability Thresholds whenever we upgrade our safeguards.
paraphrase: Reconsidering the entire list of Capability Thresholds upon each safeguard upgrade is seen as more practical.

paraphrase: The v2.2 update excludes both sophisticated insiders and state-compromised insiders from the ASL-3 Security Standard.

paraphrase: Previously, exclusion applied only to highly sophisticated state-compromised insiders.

excerpt: The model capabilities and threat models corresponding with the ASL-3 Security Standard do not warrant protection against either group: the CBRN-3 threat models entail large numbers of users having access to unguarded models (which is more likely to occur through a universal jailbreak than via model theft), and the relatively small number of employees who might be capable of model theft does not significantly affect the risk level.
paraphrase: ASL-3 threat models do not warrant protection against these insider groups, since CBRN-3 risk more likely arises from jailbreaks than model theft, and few employees could plausibly steal weights.

excerpt: For AI R&D-4, the threat models generally do not depend on model weight theft and instead entail AI systems engaging in autonomous internal sabotage.
paraphrase: AI R&D-4 threat models center on autonomous internal sabotage rather than weight theft.
